context: Begin with w0: inspect current ClickHouse adapter/factory aliases, remote auth and tenancy policy, and the deployed configuration contract. Choose and record whether port/secure are removed from MCP entirely or resolved from an approved server-side profile. Implement the smallest policy-preserving change across synchronous and durable paths. Add tests that reject arbitrary port and secure overrides, prove the configured host/port/TLS tuple is unchanged, ensure validation errors do not echo secrets or raw endpoint details, and cover every accepted ClickHouse platform alias. Update the MCP reference and remote-security documentation to make the server-owned boundary explicit. Do not broaden host or credential handling.
description: Fix the PR #1465 security defect where MCP callers can set ClickHouse port and secure values even though the contract says callers cannot change destinations or tenant-owned connection state. The ClickHouse adapter uses port directly for the connection target and secure directly for transport, so arbitrary values can probe another listener on the configured host or downgrade a server-owned TLS policy. Revalidate the threat model for clickhouse, clickhouse-server, and legacy selectors before choosing the fix. The default must be fail-closed for remote authenticated tenants; a nonstandard server port may be supported only through a server-owned profile or an explicitly approved immutable value, never an arbitrary request field.

anti_patterns.dont: Keep arbitrary port and secure fields merely because they are bounded or non-secret strings
anti_patterns.instead: Resolve both from server-owned configuration or reject them at the MCP boundary.
anti_patterns.why: A port is part of a destination and secure is transport policy; numeric/string validation does not enforce tenant isolation.

anti_patterns.dont: Test only the schema error for one platform spelling
anti_patterns.instead: Exercise every supported alias and both normal and durable execution paths.
anti_patterns.why: ClickHouse has canonical names and compatibility aliases that can reach different factory paths.

anti_patterns.dont: Use live credentials or scan real internal ports in tests
anti_patterns.instead: Use fake adapter clients and assert the exact server-owned connection tuple.
anti_patterns.why: That would make a security regression suite unsafe and nondeterministic.

preserves.behavior: All error responses and telemetry remain free of passwords, tokens, raw endpoint values, and caller-controlled secrets.
ClickHouse local mode remains in-process and does not gain a network path as a side effect of the fix.
Credentials, hostnames, DSNs, filesystem paths, and transport policy remain server-owned and are never accepted from MCP request arguments.
Durable retries cannot reintroduce rejected raw request mappings.
